items.subject: Implement the LrC plug-in as the diagram designs it
items.detail: **Terry, 2026-08-18, cleared hot for this session.** The Auth Data Flow panel is the specification: 32 steps, plug-in first, from `Authorize with FGA` through `POST /api/v001/*`. **The premise is CONFIRMED at runtime** -- a third-party plug-in can enumerate Adobe's Flickr publish service and read `getRemoteId()`, measured on LrC 15.5 against Terry's real catalog. See `docs/LRC-CLIENT-NOTES.md` and its *PICK UP HERE*, `lightroom-plugin-sdk-facts` and `lrc-plugin-dev-mechanics` in memory. **ADR-23 refuses `LrUUID` for credentials, ADR-24 makes the confirmation page a requirement, and ADR-25 governs the version gate.** The diagram's route names are still a PROPOSAL the code does not serve -- that has to be settled before or during this

items.subject: Build the backend API the diagram designs
items.detail: **Terry, 2026-08-18, cleared hot for this session.** Whatever the Worker needs so the Auth Data Flow panel is TRUE rather than proposed. **The route rename LANDED 2026-08-18**: `src/` now serves `/auth/device-link/{start,poll,approve,deny}` and `/auth/flickr/{login,callback,logout}`, 71 replacements across 11 files, gate green and all 46 mutations caught. **It removed a real fragility** -- `start` used to be credential-free only because `deviceRoutes` mounted before `apiRoutes`' blanket `requireSession` on `/api/v001/*`, and an exemption bought by registration order is invisible in the route it protects. **What REMAINS: `enter-user-code`.** The diagram draws it inside the Worker; the code serves that page from the SPA at `/link`, because `verificationUri` is `new URL("/link", UI_ORIGIN)`. **Both readings are defensible and Terry holds the pen** -- see `DIAGRAM-NOTES.md`, *"ONE route label is still a proposal"*. Pairs with the plug-in row: two ends of one flow, ADR-18 lockstep

items.subject: Bring the JAMstack client onto the same flow as the plug-in
items.detail: **Terry, 2026-08-18, cleared hot for this session.** The Svelte app of ADR-18 works the same way as the LrC plug-in client. **ADR-18 already says these are TWO first-class clients released in LOCKSTEP** -- an API change that serves one and breaks the other is a broken release, not a follow-up. **The canvas is currently scoped to the plug-in journey on purpose**, because two first-class clients drawn as line-of-flow made the drawing a mesh; see `DIAGRAM-NOTES.md`, *"the canvas is scoped to the Lightroom Classic journey"*. So this item has a diagram consequence to settle as well as code. Depends on the backend row above

items.subject: Make the 8.5x14 export actually BE 8.5x14
items.detail: **Terry, 2026-08-18, restating the ask:** the PDF and PNG come out at the right ASPECT RATIO but not at legal size, so printing needs *Fit on page* and *"it's minor but feels stupid"*. **He wants the annoyance gone**, and is open to any route -- including a new drawing space that IS 8.5x14 with the geometry airlifted across and scaled down proportionally, since the drop is 11 in to 8.5 in of height. Today the sheet carries `pageScale` 1.3165, and draw.io sizes an exported page as `pageWidth * pageScale`, which is where the 18.43 x 11.19 in comes from. **The refusal to rescale geometry is a real constraint** -- every font size and every threshold in the check suite would stop meaning what it means -- so a solution has to keep the AUTHORED canvas at 11x17 and do any scaling on the way out. See `DIAGRAM-NOTES.md`, *"SETTLED 2026-08-17"*, which this supersedes

items.subject: Make the 16x9 sheet native 4K at 100%
items.detail: The page IS 3840 x 2160 now, not an export percentage -- **native means nobody types a zoom number**, and a forgotten export dialog is exactly the step that goes wrong once and is never noticed. The scaling machinery row 7 built carried it: `Sheet.scale_up` in `diagram_sheets.py` lifts the "never grow the content" cap for this sheet alone, and the content is 1640 x 1040 of ink against a 3760 x 2080 printable area, so the scale is **exactly 2.0000** and 10.1 pt body type lands on 20.2 px. **Lifting that cap everywhere would have grown the AUTHORED tabloid drawing**, which is why it is per-sheet. Margin went 20 -> 40 with the sheet, keeping the same proportion of picture to gutter. The build reports this sheet in pixels and says `SCREEN` rather than `EXPORT ... in`, because calling a 3840-unit page 38.40 in is a category error. Rendered and looked at. Gate green, 297 tests

items.subject: Spike: can Trello be the work log?
items.detail: **Answered in `docs/TRELLO-SPIKE-NOTES.md`, and tier 1 came back better than either of us expected.** `atlassian/trello-mcp-server` is an OFFICIAL remote MCP server at `https://mcp.trello.com/v1`, OAuth 2.0, workspace-scoped, nine weeks old -- which is why Terry's search found only third-party ones. It ships an official `trello-use` skill, and it **cannot permanently delete anything**, which matches an append-only log rather than fighting it. Tiers 2 and 3 are thin: Atlassian publishes NO Trello Python library (`atlassian-python-api` is community and carries zero Trello files), and `py-trello` last shipped 2024-06-11. REST is public and live; the GraphQL endpoint exists, is undocumented, and refuses arbitrary queries like a persisted-query-only internal transport -- **MUST NOT be built on**. **SETTLED 2026-08-18: Terry connected it, saw what the grant actually does, and shut it off.** Standing order, verbatim: *"do not read OR write from trello."* **The blocker is identity** -- the OAuth grant makes Claude the USER, not a bot member: `get_me` returned `terrydott`. So a private board is not a boundary (privacy limits which PEOPLE see it, and Claude is an owner), the grant reached all 25 boards in `Terry Personal`, and **a card Claude moves is indistinguishable from a card Terry moves** -- which kills the signoff design on its own terms. **The escape route was surveyed and Terry closed it.** Single-board guests really are free and unlimited on a paid workspace, so a bot account on one board would have bought a real boundary AND real attribution -- but **Trello has no service-account concept**, so a bot identity means a second human-shaped account with a real email and a verification click. Terry, 2026-08-18: *"I don't think I can create an NPE account."* **A rejected middle option is recorded too:** publishing the log as a private claude.ai Artifact for phone reading. He refused it -- *"I like our private website best"* -- and an Artifact is a SNAPSHOT rather than a live read, so it would have reintroduced the two-views divergence he calls worse than having no list. **What Trello would genuinely have added is INBOUND: queueing cards for Claude from his phone.** His own answer: *"claude remote control was working"* -- he messages Claude directly, which the read-only viewer was never going to do. **`docs/WORK-LOG.md` remains the single source of truth, and `scripts/worklog-server.py` at `http://127.0.0.1:8792/` remains the only view**

items.subject: Spike: can an LrC plug-in publish PNG to Flickr?
items.detail: **Answered in `docs/PNG-PUBLISH-SPIKE-NOTES.md`. YES on both halves, and Terry's belief about Adobe's plug-in is right.** `Sample Plugins/flickr.lrdevplugin/FlickrExportServiceProvider.lua` declares `allowFileFormats = { 'JPEG' }`, and that one line is the whole restriction -- the SDK's own reference lists `JPEG PSD PSB TIFF DNG PNG JXL AVIF ORIGINAL` as legal members. A plug-in MAY also pin `exportSettings.LR_format` outright. Flickr's help page, updated a month ago, lists PNG with **no conversion note**, while TIFF and BMP are *"converted to & saved as a JPEG"* -- **so on Flickr, PNG is the ONLY lossless format**, and TIFF would look like it worked while delivering the exact loss he is avoiding. **The real constraint is the 200 MB per-photo cap**: an R5 frame is 44.8 Mpx, so 8-bit PNG lands near 96-122 MB and fits, while 16-bit lands near 192-243 MB and probably does not. **Those are estimates and need one real export to settle.** Separate plug-in from FGA's, which never uploads a byte

items.subject: Build the shared work-log web view
items.detail: **Terry's signoff, verbatim: *"let's sign off on that local service and cut over."*** `scripts/worklog-server.py` serves this file at `http://127.0.0.1:8792/`, repainting within 400 ms of every write. It parses through `scripts/worklog.py`, shared with `worklog-sync-check.py`, so the two readers cannot drift. `Hide landed` defaults on and sticks per browser. **It reads the file rather than a copy, which is the whole point** -- the sync problem exists only where there are two copies. **This is the FIRST row to cross the signoff edge**, and the first use of this table
